subject: Regional network partition: action checklist and audit requests for affected customers (EU & APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Acme Retail Ops <ops@acme-retail.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2029-12-17T08:12:00Z
Subject: Observed network partition — EU & APAC traffic spike / suggested customer-level reroute

Team / Acme ops,

We are seeing a network partition between our EU/APAC edge clusters and several cloud egress points originating ~08:00 UTC. Symptoms: increased 502/504 errors for short-lived requests and higher tail latency on APAC customers, and failed TLS handshakes for a subset of EU subnets. Root cause still under investigation with cloud provider but impact window is ongoing.

Immediate mitigation recommendation (customer-facing):
- For affected customers (Acme Retail, Orion Logistics): enable forced-region-fallback to US-central for requests that do not contain PII flags.
- Enable sidecar prefix-caching (config: sidecar.cache.prefix=true) for long-running streams to reduce retry pressure.
- Apply temporary rate-limits on non-critical background jobs to free capacity for real-time inference.

I've attached a short reroute playbook with CLI snippets and a mapping of customer routes. Please implement these steps for Acme and confirm once done.

Attachments: reroute_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF)

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Retail Ops <ops@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2029-12-17T08:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed network partition — EU & APAC traffic spike / suggested customer-level reroute

Marissa — thanks, forwarding to ops. Quick questions before we flip any customer-level controls:

1) Can you produce a per-tenant impact table (error rate, p50/p95 latency, % traffic affected) for the last 60m?
2) Do we recommend forcing fallback at the router (RT) layer or at the model selection layer? I want to avoid cross-region KV cache misses if possible.
3) If Acme asks to enable auto-fallback for all production traffic, what's our rollback plan?

I can start the mapping and run the CLI commands if you paste the exact flags. Pinging Jonas for infra-side permissions.

Karthik
Head of Customer Reliability
karthik@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Acme Retail Ops <ops@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2029-12-17T08:41:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed network partition — EU & APAC traffic spike / suggested customer-level reroute

On 2029-12-17 08:28, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Marissa — thanks, forwarding to ops. Quick questions before we flip any customer-level controls:
>
> 1) Can you produce a per-tenant impact table (error rate, p50/p95 latency, % traffic affected) for the last 60m?

Attached is a quick snapshot for Acme Retail (see acme_audit_snapshot_20291217.json). Key points for Acme:
- error rate: 6.8% overall in last 60m, APAC nodes 13.1%
- p95 latency (inference): APAC 1.48s; EU 0.93s
- % traffic affected: estimated 18% of token-requests routed via impacted egress points

Recommended flags to run (example):
- redwoodctl customer set-route --customer acme-retail --region us-central --force=true
- redwoodctl sidecar update --name acme-sidecar --set sidecar.cache.prefix=true

Rollback: run redwoodctl customer set-route --customer acme-retail --region auto

I've also created HubSpot ticket HS-58421 and a support case in PagerDuty for infra escalation. Please confirm when you execute the CLI so I can update the playbook.

Attachments: acme_audit_snapshot_20291217.json (JSON)

Marissa
From: Acme Retail Ops <ops@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-retail.com
Date: 2029-12-17T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed network partition — EU & APAC traffic spike / suggested customer-level reroute

Thanks Marissa — we appreciate the snapshot and the playbook. Two asks from our side:
1) Our security team needs the TLS handshake failure logs and an export of request-level audit logs for the 07:50–08:30 UTC window. Can you provide a signed export or S3 link?
2) If we move critical inference to us-central, can you confirm whether there will be any SLA credit or short-term contractual remedy?

We will stand by to apply the redwoodctl commands once we get confirmation and the audit export.

— Alex Martinez
Site Reliability Lead, Acme Retail
ops@acme-retail.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Acme Retail Ops <ops@acme-retail.com>

Subject: Re: Observed network partition — EU & APAC traffic spike / suggested customer-level reroute

Alex — short answers: we will provide the audit export and a preliminary credit offer. Action plan: 

- Marissa/Infra: generate signed S3 export of TLS logs + request-level traces for Acme (07:50–08:30 UTC). Use S3 bucket redwood-customer-exports/acme/2029-12-17/ and mark with HS-58421.
- Commercial: offer 2 days of service credit for the window as a gesture while we complete RCA. Legal/commercial to confirm exact wording, I’ll own it.
- Follow-up: full postmortem and timeline by EOD; RCA team (Jonas) to lead main incident analysis.

Jonas, can you confirm infra timeline for the export? Karthik, please coordinate with Acme for the temporary route change and monitor KV cache behavior post-fallback.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Commercial Ops
